title: Spin-Charge Conversion in an Epitaxial Kagome Flat-Band Metal
authors: Wenyi Zhou, Yuqing Zhu, Katherine Johnson, Hari Paudyal, Duy Nguyen, Dimitri King, Jaden Ma, Jay A. Gupta, Michael E. Flatte, Roland K. Kawakami
abstract: The formation of topological flat bands near the Fermi level in kagome-structured metals has generated substantial research interest. One key consequence of this electronic structure is the strong anisotropy in charge transport, such as the significantly higher in-plane resistivity relative to the out-of-plane direction. However, the spin transport properties of these flat-band kagome metals are still largely unexplored. In this work, we investigate spin-charge conversion in CoSn, a representative flat-band kagome metal. Scanning tunneling microscopy is employed to image the CoSn surface with atomic resolution, and $dI/dV$ spectroscopy shows clear signatures of the flat bands. Using magneto-optical techniques, we quantify the spin-orbit torque (SOT) in bilayers of ferromagnetic nickel (Ni) and c-plane CoSn thin films. We find a large effective spin Hall angle of $θ_{SH} = 0.484 \pm 0.005$ within the CoSn layers, significantly exceeding the value measured for Pt of $θ_{SH} = 0.0436 \pm 0.0003$ in Ni/Pt bilayers. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations provide a microscopic understanding of the intrinsic spin Hall effect in CoSn, elucidating the sources of Berry curvature in momentum space. These findings establish kagome metals as promising materials for efficient spin-charge conversion and low-power spintronics.
summary: This work demonstrates highly efficient spin-charge conversion in epitaxial CoSn, a Kagome flat-band metal, by measuring a large spin Hall angle. The findings, supported by DFT calculations elucidating Berry curvature, establish these materials as superior candidates for next-generation, low-power spintronic devices.
main_problem: The study investigates the often-unexplored spin transport properties and spin-charge conversion efficiency in epitaxial Kagome flat-band metals.
main_result: The authors found a significantly large effective spin Hall angle ($	heta_{SH} = 0.484$) in CoSn, substantially exceeding that of control materials like Pt, establishing Kagome metals as promising candidates for low-power spintronics.
method: The research combines experimental measurements (STM, magneto-optical torque measurements) with theoretical calculations (DFT) to characterize spin-orbit coupling effects.
model_or_system: The primary system is CoSn, a flat-band Kagome metal, studied in epitaxial thin films, often configured in bilayers with ferromagnetic metals like Ni.
key_observables: Effective spin Hall angle ($	heta_{SH}$), Spin-Orbit Torque (SOT), spin Berry curvature components ($\Omega$), and intrinsic Spin Hall Conductivity (SHC) tensor components ($\sigma$).
important_parameters: The high anisotropy of charge transport (in-plane vs. out-of-plane resistivity) and the comparison between $	heta_{SH}$ in CoSn vs. Pt are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The intrinsic SHC calculation is noted to be limited in direct comparison to the measured effective $	heta_{SH}$ due to unmodeled interface and extrinsic effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the atomic structure and electronic signatures (STM/dI/dV) of CoSn, alongside theoretical plots showing the momentum dependence of spin Berry curvature and the energy dependence of intrinsic SHC components.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from characterizing the electronic structure (flat bands via STM/DFT) to measuring the spin-charge conversion efficiency (SOT measurements) and finally providing a microscopic understanding of the enhancement via DFT calculations of Berry curvature and SHC.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism/spintronics, the strong coupling between electronic structure (flat bands, Berry curvature) and transport properties provides a rich platform for understanding topological effects in quantum materials, which has parallels to topological quantum computing concepts.
